name: Quest Representatives
description: Which AI representative holds each quest and handles each request, task and newly assigned goal.
purpose: Put each request in the hands of the representative that fits it.
approach: Choose by assignment, role, thread and the quests each representative holds, keep a thread's representative for the work it spawns, and ask the person only when two fit equally.
out_of_scope: What the representative does with the request; the hub's The Representatives owns the general seat.
milestones: 1. Assigned representatives, threads, reassignment and new-goal owners pass on labelled cases.
measures_of_success: On labelled requests the chosen representative matches the label, work spawned from a thread keeps its representative, and the person is asked only when two fit equally.
parameters: The roles, assignments and visibility of each representative.
inputs: A message, a queued task, a new goal or an autopilot pass, with the quest.
effects: None beyond recording who holds the work.
usage_notes: Reached by the host before the request is planned.

name: Scoped recent-context warm start
description: Keeps each work item's recent cards available to the next turn at no model cost, fenced so one work item's records never reach another.
purpose: Hands the next turn of a conversation the cards its last turns already found, so a short follow-up needs no restating.
approach: Stores each turn's selected cards under the work item's key and returns the relevant ones at the start of the next turn.
out_of_scope: Finding cards by meaning, and a follow-up that shares no words with the earlier turns it refers to.
milestones: 1. Every synthetic multi-turn follow-up case returns the right earlier cards, and no stale or cross-work-item card is returned.
knowledge: Cards are re-selected from scratch each turn under a short budget, so a follow-up paid full cost and a timeout left a turn with nothing. Scope tags fence one work item's records from another's, while untagged legacy records stay visible. A purely lexical gate misses a paraphrase that shares no word, which is a known limit.
measures_of_success: On synthetic multi-turn cases the right earlier cards come back for a follow-up, and no stale or cross-work-item card is ever returned. Standing conditions: Keep stale and cross-work-item cards from being returned. Spend no model call.
parameters: The file store takes a root directory and caps for turns, cards, preview length, record age and items per card, with separate larger caps for the global scope. Scope keys name a conversation, a work item or the global scope.
inputs: For record: scope keys, the selected cards and the user's text. For load: scope keys, then the current turn's text for filtering.
outputs: Recent card records merged across scopes, narrower scope winning, deduplicated by card id, then filtered by relevance, with optional item-usage hints and rendered blocks.
effects: Writes small per-scope files atomically. Both calls are best effort and never raise.
usage_notes: Record after each turn that selected cards and load at the start of the next. Always pass the work item's key so the fence applies, and treat the result as a warm fallback beside, not instead of, normal retrieval.

name: Incremental context-update feed
description: Tells an assistant what is new on a work item since it last looked, drawing on notes, goal updates and decisions, and offers each person's item once without echoing the assistant's own words back.
purpose: Help an assistant catch up on a work item where people left off, so it answers what is new and open and not what it has already seen.
approach: Collect the items added to a work item since the assistant last looked and mark which of them ask for something.
out_of_scope: Finding older background that is not new since the last look, and deciding when standing work starts (Proactivity does that) or what matters first (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. The exact set of offered items and open asks matches the stated rules on the synthetic quests, with the age and count bounds holding. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A live run once treated a habit log and a daily reflection as asks and later reported them as still owed, so channels declare whether they carry asks. A reply written after a note is not proof the note was handled, and an assistant hearing its own words echoed back wastes budget. Card-scoped channels are relevant by where they were written, while user-scoped ones need a relevance judgment.
measures_of_success: The exact set of offered items and open asks matches the stated rules on synthetic quests: own words in, assistant echoes and unattributed notes out, answered and seen items not repeated, bounds respected. Standing conditions: Keep age and count bounds holding.
parameters: A source declares a name, a one-line description, and flags for whether its items need a relevance judgment, an admission judgment, tracking as asks, or relaying onto the work item. The engine takes the sources to watch, the channels always checked, and a clock; a collect call takes the item, an optional since time and the delivered-run history.
inputs: A collect request naming the work item and the time of the last look, plus whatever the channel's client returns (notes, goal updates, decisions, and similar).
outputs: A bundle of context updates, each with an item id, its text and author, and whether it needs a response, plus the set of open asks.
effects: Advances the watermark of what has been seen and may record asks for later tracking. Sources never raise: a source that fails reports an empty result and says why.
usage_notes: Call at the start of a turn or task for a work item and render the bundle into the prompt. Add a channel by implementing the source interface and setting its flags honestly, since a wrong asks flag turns a person's diary into owed answers.

name: Context card persistence backend
description: Stores context cards durably in whichever place they must live, with the same behaviour in a local folder, a vector database or the Quest backend.
purpose: Keeps context cards safe and retrievable wherever a person needs them to live, from a local folder to the Quest backend.
approach: Writes, reads, lists and deletes context cards in the chosen store, with no card lost and none duplicated.
out_of_scope: Deciding which cards suit a turn, and backend-specific logic in card handling.
milestones: 1. The same 14 conformance cases pass on the filesystem, embedded Qdrant and Quest API backends. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The same conformance cases pass against a Qdrant server and the dev Quest API, not only the embedded and fake backends.
knowledge: Persistence is a boundary: card logic lives in the store and a backend only stores and fetches. A listing that silently truncated at a page limit once made a backend fail the volume case. Backend errors must be loud and counted, not swallowed, and card identity is the pair of scope and id so the same id may exist privately and in a team.
measures_of_success: Every conformance case passes on every backend: round trip, overwrite, no loss at volume and across pages, no duplicate, delete including after restart, concurrent writers, change stamp and tolerance of bad input. Standing conditions: Lose no card, create no duplicate, and behave the same on every backend, including after restart, under concurrent writers and across paged listings.
parameters: Backend choice and connection (folder path; vector collection, embedder and vector size or server url; Quest base url, key, timeout and scope), plus the optional scope used for tenant isolation.
inputs: Card ids and card dictionaries for write (a card as defined in docs/explanation/context-assembly.md, What a context card is: id, name, keywords, summary and description, pinned files, typed content references, provenance, usage, scope tags and origin); ids for read, delete and exists.
outputs: Load-all returns a mapping of id to card, read returns a card or nothing, write and delete return success flags, and revision returns a change stamp used to invalidate caches.
effects: Durable writes to the chosen store (atomic files, vector points embedded at write time, or API calls), and for the API backend logged and counted errors.
usage_notes: Pick the backend by where the cards must live and inject it into the card store; every backend must pass the same conformance cases, so none is better when it conforms. Add a backend by implementing the protocol and a harness. A card's fields, its id rules and what is not a card are defined once in docs/explanation/context-assembly.md, What a context card is; docs/how-to/context-card-stores.md covers stores, mounts and copies.

name: Feedback-to-guidance loop
description: Keeps a person's corrections as standing guidance, apart from one-off requests, and shows each one on the turns where it applies.
purpose: Help the assistant stop repeating a mistake a person has already corrected, so they only have to say it once.
approach: Turn each correction into guidance kept apart from one-off requests and shown where it bears on the turn.
out_of_scope: One-off requests, which are not promoted to permanent rules.
milestones: 1. After a standing correction is stored, the next relevant turn shows it, and no correction that does not bear on the turn is shown, across the feedback sequences.
knowledge: Remembering everything gives perfect recall but turns one-time requests into permanent rules and crowds every prompt, so a ledger separating standing from one-off corrections is needed. The current weakness is precision: with no relevance cut below the card limit, an unrelated rule is shown while room remains. Guidance enters the system prompt as behaviour to follow, not optional context.
measures_of_success: After a standing correction is stored, the next relevant turn shows it, corrections that do not bear on the turn are not shown, and one-off requests are not promoted.
parameters: Cards directory, optional dynamic guidance loader, vector store, provider and model for relevance filtering, a card manager factory, and the number of cards selected per turn.
inputs: A user message and caller scope metadata for selection; correction text, author, location and run dispositions for the ledger.
outputs: A list of guidance cards with bodies for the applicable-guidance block; a catalog and single card reads on demand.
effects: The ledger records observations and writes guidance cards on standing corrections; selection itself is read-only; never raises.
usage_notes: Wire the provider into the orchestrator so selection runs once before planning; rank by relevance when the card limit has room, add a vector or model filter where precision matters.

name: Guidance toward the long-term goal
description: Decides when and how a reply points the person at their quest's next milestone and its current metric reading, at the intent level that fits the moment (the goal in focus, the quest, or a representative's portfolio), and when it stays silent.
purpose: Keeps the person moving toward the end they are working for, without hijacking a simple question or nagging.
approach: The reply voice answers first. A directive about the long-term goal is added to it, saying when to add one short pointer, at which level, with the real milestone and reading, and when to leave it out; a grader checks both sides on labelled cases.
out_of_scope: Choosing the milestone or the metric (the quest and its intent hold them), creating or linking intents (only a person does), and the representative's standing view (hold-the-intents).
milestones: 1. The two-sided metric has a case set and a recorded result for the floor, the current reply voice and the guided arm. 2. The guided arm beats the current reply voice on the two-sided value, with no invented figure and no more awkward restraint cases.
knowledge: Proposed 2026-10-29 from the 2026-10-27 accountability meeting transcript (spiritual_data_funding/human_context/meetings/transcripts/2026-10-27-accountability-meeting-1JByS08XMyrA7HJk5rVpRQaRJqG29wMyzUk9QfHMba8k.txt, 49:15 to 50:27) and the 2026-10-28 excerpt (hierarchy of intents, 24:44 to 25:50). The direction: the assistant should generally encourage the person to move forward on the long-term goal, thinking in ESOI terms, aware of the next target milestone and the current metric, at whatever intent level makes sense for the context, and the metric must also catch awkward use of it.
measures_of_success: Nudge cases right and restraint cases right rise together, per intent level. Standing conditions: Never invent a milestone, date or figure. Answer the request first. Add no model call before the reply.
parameters: The directive text, the word limit of the reply and the model tier.
inputs: The quest, its next milestone and metric reading, the intent hierarchy it sits under (or, for a representative, its assigned quests), the conversation so far, and the message.
outputs: The reply, with or without one short pointer.
effects: None beyond the reply text; no added call.
usage_notes: Selected: guided_v2 (the LONG_TERM_GUIDANCE section of REPLY_VOICE_SYSTEM). reply_voice is the reply voice before it, guided the first candidate directive, no_nudge the floor.

name: Goal assignee and doability judge
description: Decides the verdicts on who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI representative can take it over, with a model call that is kept only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives a person the verdicts on who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI representative can take it over at a cost and delay that its metric accepts.
approach: A prompt declared as a prompt spec makes one model call to decide who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI can take it over.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier (choose-a-model-tier) and the surrounding turn or run.
milestones: 1. Its metric has a case set and a recorded result for the current arm and the no-model floor. 2. The model call stays only while it beats the floor on the metric.
knowledge: Proposed 2026-10-28 so that this prompt has a solution and a metric that justify its cost, time and value; not built, so the metric is unmeasured and the current call is a direction, not a measured win.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from the cases without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: The model tier and any cap the module states.
inputs: The text or events the call is given.
outputs: The text or verdict the call returns.
effects: One model call; no write beyond the text it returns.
usage_notes: Selected today: model_judge. The floor is a proposed arm with no model call. Decision teamdec_f95b130faacd (cases relabelled).
